title: Zuse: the European decision model
excerpt: Typed decisions with calibrated probabilities, in 27 European languages and many more. Hosted in the EU.
content_html:
Meet Zuse, the decision model.Like Jev, but built and hosted in Europe.

Zuse reads a document, picks from the options you set and tells you how sure it is.

Zuse in numbers

Tested on tasks it never trained on, and against the chat models you already know.

65,536
tokens per document on the API, about 100 pages of text

0.2 s
typical time to answer through the API, every question at once

1.6%
gap between how sure it says it is and how often it is right

How it works

  1. 1Send the documentAn email, a form, a clause, a case note, in 27 European languages and many more.
  2. 2Ask your questionsWrite any question and list the answers it may pick from: yes or no, a scale, or up to 255 options.
  3. 3Act on the answerEach answer comes with how sure Zuse is, so you choose which ones to act on automatically.

What can you use Zuse for?

Anywhere a person reads something and picks from a fixed set of answers.

Customer service

Questions

What is Zuse?

A model that reads a document and answers your questions about it with a short answer, picked from options you choose, and tells you how sure it is. Use it to sort emails, check forms, flag urgent cases and more.

How is Zuse different from a chat model?

A chat model writes a long answer that you then have to read and check, and you pay for every word. Zuse picks from the answers you give it and says how sure it is. It never writes text of its own, so it is faster and cheaper, and it cannot wander off topic.

How does Zuse compare with Jev?

It answers the same kind of questions as TypeSafe's Jev, with the same request and response format. On Jev's own public English benchmark, Zuse 27B matches its accuracy (86.0% against 85.7% published) and can safely automate more decisions: 77.6% against 70.0%, with half as many confident mistakes. And it runs in the EU, is trained on 27 European languages and comes with a data processing agreement.

Zuse and Jev side by side, and how to move your Jev code →
Which languages does it support?

115 of the 210 languages we tested score 85% or more, 49 of them European: Afrikaans, Albanian, Arabic, Armenian, Assamese, Asturian, Awadhi, Azerbaijani, Banjar, Basque, Belarusian, Bengali, Bhojpuri, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Cantonese, Catalan, Cebuano, Chhattisgarhi, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Crimean Tatar, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dari, Dutch, Egyptian Arabic, English, Esperanto, Estonian, Faroese, Finnish, French, Galician, Georgian, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kannada, Kashmiri (Arabic script), Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Latvian, Levantine Arabic, Ligurian, Limburgish, Lithuanian, Lombard, Luxembourgish, Macedonian, Magahi, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Marathi, Mesopotamian Arabic, Minangkabau, Najdi Arabic, Nepali, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, Occitan, Odia, Papiamento, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Samoan, Sanskrit, Sardinian, Scottish Gaelic, Serbian, Sicilian, Sinhala, Slovak, Slovenian, South Azerbaijani, South Levantine Arabic, Spanish, Sundanese, Swahili, Swedish, Ta'izzi-Adeni Arabic, Tagalog, Tajik, Tamil, Tatar, Telugu, Thai, Tok Pisin, Tunisian Arabic, Turkish, Turkmen, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uyghur, Uzbek, Venetian, Vietnamese, Welsh, Yiddish. Zuse was trained on 27 European languages; the rest comes from its base model. Just under the bar: Friulian (83%), Silesian (83%), Latgalian (80%).

How accurate is it?

On 20,044 questions in 27 languages, from tasks it never trained on, Zuse 27B answers 87.5% correctly. On routing, reading and sentiment it is right 90 to 95% of the time. Every answer comes with how sure Zuse is, so you can act automatically on the ones it is sure about.

Which model should we choose?

Zuse 27B is the most accurate, for the decisions you automate. Zuse 9B is faster and cheaper, for sorting at high volume. Both use the same API and the same key, so you can start with one and switch.

What does it cost?

You pay only for the text Zuse reads. It writes no text, so there are no output tokens to pay for: a decision on a one-page document costs a fraction of a cent. Prices for each model are in the pricing section above.

Where is it hosted, and what happens to our data?

Zuse runs on servers in the EU (Spain, Germany or Sweden, and another EU region when GPU capacity requires it). Your documents and questions are not stored, not logged and never used for training; we keep only metadata: token counts and cost for billing, and counts such as the number of questions and the document's language. Our data processing agreement and list of subprocessors are at bineric.com/legal.

Can we run it on our own servers?

Yes. A dedicated instance reserves a GPU in an EU data centre for you alone, with its own endpoint, and we can also run Zuse on your own servers. Talk to us and we will price it for your volume.

When should we check its answers?

Set a confidence level per question and look at anything below it. Routing, reading and sentiment automate well; legal, grammar and general-knowledge questions are better checked. Do not use Zuse alone for decisions about a person's employment, credit, benefits or legal rights.

Easy to get started with Zuse

Get an API key, send a document and your questions, and the answers come straight back.

问题

What is Zuse?

A model that reads a document and answers your questions about it with a short answer, picked from options you choose, and tells you how sure it is. Use it to sort emails, check forms, flag urgent cases and more.

How is Zuse different from a chat model?

A chat model writes a long answer that you then have to read and check, and you pay for every word. Zuse picks from the answers you give it and says how sure it is. It never writes text of its own, so it is faster and cheaper, and it cannot wander off topic.

How does Zuse compare with Jev?

It answers the same kind of questions as TypeSafe's Jev, with the same request and response format. On Jev's own public English benchmark, Zuse 27B matches its accuracy (86.0% against 85.7% published) and can safely automate more decisions: 77.6% against 70.0%, with half as many confident mistakes. And it runs in the EU, is trained on 27 European languages and comes with a data processing agreement.

Zuse and Jev side by side, and how to move your Jev code →
Which languages does it support?

115 of the 210 languages we tested score 85% or more, 49 of them European: Afrikaans, Albanian, Arabic, Armenian, Assamese, Asturian, Awadhi, Azerbaijani, Banjar, Basque, Belarusian, Bengali, Bhojpuri, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Cantonese, Catalan, Cebuano, Chhattisgarhi, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Crimean Tatar, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dari, Dutch, Egyptian Arabic, English, Esperanto, Estonian, Faroese, Finnish, French, Galician, Georgian, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kannada, Kashmiri (Arabic script), Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Latvian, Levantine Arabic, Ligurian, Limburgish, Lithuanian, Lombard, Luxembourgish, Macedonian, Magahi, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Marathi, Mesopotamian Arabic, Minangkabau, Najdi Arabic, Nepali, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, Occitan, Odia, Papiamento, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Samoan, Sanskrit, Sardinian, Scottish Gaelic, Serbian, Sicilian, Sinhala, Slovak, Slovenian, South Azerbaijani, South Levantine Arabic, Spanish, Sundanese, Swahili, Swedish, Ta'izzi-Adeni Arabic, Tagalog, Tajik, Tamil, Tatar, Telugu, Thai, Tok Pisin, Tunisian Arabic, Turkish, Turkmen, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uyghur, Uzbek, Venetian, Vietnamese, Welsh, Yiddish. Zuse was trained on 27 European languages; the rest comes from its base model. Just under the bar: Friulian (83%), Silesian (83%), Latgalian (80%).

How accurate is it?

On 20,044 questions in 27 languages, from tasks it never trained on, Zuse 27B answers 87.5% correctly. On routing, reading and sentiment it is right 90 to 95% of the time. Every answer comes with how sure Zuse is, so you can act automatically on the ones it is sure about.

Which model should we choose?

Zuse 27B is the most accurate, for the decisions you automate. Zuse 9B is faster and cheaper, for sorting at high volume. Both use the same API and the same key, so you can start with one and switch.

What does it cost?

You pay only for the text Zuse reads. It writes no text, so there are no output tokens to pay for: a decision on a one-page document costs a fraction of a cent. Prices for each model are in the pricing section above.

Where is it hosted, and what happens to our data?

Zuse runs on servers in the EU (Spain, Germany or Sweden, and another EU region when GPU capacity requires it). Your documents and questions are not stored, not logged and never used for training; we keep only metadata: token counts and cost for billing, and counts such as the number of questions and the document's language. Our data processing agreement and list of subprocessors are at bineric.com/legal.

Can we run it on our own servers?

是的。 A dedicated instance reserves a GPU in an EU data centre for you alone, with its own endpoint, and we can also run Zuse on your own servers. Talk to us and we will price it for your volume.

When should we check its answers?

Set a confidence level per question and look at anything below it. Routing, reading and sentiment automate well; legal, grammar and general-knowledge questions are better checked. Do not use Zuse alone for decisions about a person's employment, credit, benefits or legal rights.
